Lab 9 - Morphological Operations¶

Objective: apply erosion, dilation, opening and closing to a new binary image (Balls) and study how the shape and size of the structuring element change the result.

In [1]:
import cv2
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

imgFile = 'Balls_1_.png'   # upload this file next to the notebook (Colab: left sidebar > Files)

# Load as grayscale
img = cv2.imread(imgFile, 0)

# Binarize with Otsu. THRESH_BINARY_INV makes the balls WHITE (foreground = 255),
# because morphology treats white pixels as the object.
_, binary = cv2.threshold(img, 0, 255, cv2.THRESH_BINARY_INV + cv2.THRESH_OTSU)

plt.figure(figsize=(10, 5))
plt.subplot(1, 2, 1), plt.imshow(img, 'gray'), plt.title('Original (grayscale)'), plt.axis('off')
plt.subplot(1, 2, 2), plt.imshow(binary, 'gray'), plt.title('Binary (balls = white)'), plt.axis('off')
plt.show()
print('Image size:', binary.shape)

Image size: (1234, 1274)

Task 1: Basic morphological operations on the Balls image¶

A 15x15 square kernel is used so the effect is clearly visible on this large image (1274 x 1234 px).

In [2]:
kernel = np.ones((15, 15), np.uint8)

erosion  = cv2.erode(binary, kernel, iterations=1)
dilation = cv2.dilate(binary, kernel, iterations=1)
opening  = cv2.morphologyEx(binary, cv2.MORPH_OPEN,  kernel)   # dilate(erode(img))
closing  = cv2.morphologyEx(binary, cv2.MORPH_CLOSE, kernel)   # erode(dilate(img))

titles = ['Original Binary', 'Erosion', 'Dilation', 'Opening', 'Closing']
images = [binary, erosion, dilation, opening, closing]

plt.figure(figsize=(15, 9))
for i in range(5):
    plt.subplot(2, 3, i + 1)
    plt.imshow(images[i], 'gray')
    plt.title(titles[i])
    plt.axis('off')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

Task 2: Experiment with structuring elements¶

Three shapes (square, cross, ellipse) x three sizes (3x3, 5x5, 7x7). cv2.getStructuringElement builds each kernel. Because the image is large, 3x3 to 7x7 kernels give subtle changes, so iterations=3 is used to make the differences visible.

In [3]:
shapes = {
    'Square':  cv2.MORPH_RECT,
    'Cross':   cv2.MORPH_CROSS,
    'Ellipse': cv2.MORPH_ELLIPSE,
}
sizes = [3, 5, 7]
ITER = 3

# Show what the kernels look like
print('5x5 kernels:')
for name, shp in shapes.items():
    print(name); print(cv2.getStructuringElement(shp, (5, 5)))

5x5 kernels:

2.1 Erosion with different shapes and sizes¶

In [4]:
fig, axes = plt.subplots(3, 3, figsize=(15, 14))
for r, (name, shp) in enumerate(shapes.items()):
    for c, s in enumerate(sizes):
        k = cv2.getStructuringElement(shp, (s, s))
        out = cv2.erode(binary, k, iterations=ITER)
        axes[r, c].imshow(out, 'gray')
        axes[r, c].set_title(f'Erosion - {name} {s}x{s}')
        axes[r, c].axis('off')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

2.2 Dilation with different shapes and sizes¶

In [5]:
fig, axes = plt.subplots(3, 3, figsize=(15, 14))
for r, (name, shp) in enumerate(shapes.items()):
    for c, s in enumerate(sizes):
        k = cv2.getStructuringElement(shp, (s, s))
        out = cv2.dilate(binary, k, iterations=ITER)
        axes[r, c].imshow(out, 'gray')
        axes[r, c].set_title(f'Dilation - {name} {s}x{s}')
        axes[r, c].axis('off')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

2.3 Quantitative comparison (number of white pixels)¶

In [6]:
orig = int(np.count_nonzero(binary))
print(f'Original white pixels: {orig}\n')
print(f"{'Shape':<9}{'Size':<6}{'Erosion':>10}{'change %':>11}{'Dilation':>12}{'change %':>11}")
print('-' * 59)
for name, shp in shapes.items():
    for s in sizes:
        k = cv2.getStructuringElement(shp, (s, s))
        e = int(np.count_nonzero(cv2.erode(binary,  k, iterations=ITER)))
        d = int(np.count_nonzero(cv2.dilate(binary, k, iterations=ITER)))
        print(f'{name:<9}{str(s)+"x"+str(s):<6}{e:>10}{(e-orig)/orig*100:>10.1f}%{d:>12}{(d-orig)/orig*100:>10.1f}%')
